eligibility.quote: The timer as passed in there is not owned by the `Rate` object, it is owned by whatever is creating that (in this case, the Node is the one that calls `create_rate`).  Instead, the user should call `node.destroy_rate(rate)` to properly destroy a previously created Rate object.

Instead, the user should call `node.destroy_rate(rate)` to properly destroy a previously created Rate object.

loudness.quote: The CPU usage explodes and ros becomes laggy. I found that Rate._timer are not properly destroyed.

resolution.quote: Ok I understood how to use it now thank you. I did the same benchmark with the code below. Conclusion: Yes this works as intended and the CPU usage stays low.

notes: Eligibility is a defensible judgment call: the consumer node and rclpy interact through the library API, and the failure depends on the consumer's wrong assumption about who owns the timer (a consumer calling node.destroy_rate does not leak), so it is not internal (would not occur with any correct peer). The maintainer comment verbatim confirms the ownership rule; the reporter's follow-up comment verbatim confirms the resolved composition works. class `other` is correct: this is an ownership/lifecycle convention of a library API covered by no specific class. outcome failure (resource exhaustion) and loudness silent_documented (found only via `top`, no tooling diagnostic) are correct; detection_stage run. Resolution observed is correct: reporter confirms destroy_rate keeps CPU low with the same humble binaries.
